requirements.requirement: Persistently disable acceptance of IPv4 ICMP redirects on node1.
requirements.summary: The persistent sysctl file sets both all and default accept_redirects to 0. Before restart, all/default/enp1s0 were 0; after a confirmed reboot they remained 0, demonstrating persistence for the global policy, future interfaces, and the active external interface. The post-restart loopback-specific value was 1, but the required all/default policy and relevant routed interface were hardened.

requirements.requirement: Persistently disable acceptance of IPv4 source-routed packets on node1.
requirements.summary: The persistent sysctl file sets both all and default accept_source_route to 0. The values were 0 for all/default/enp1s0 before restart and for every enumerated IPv4 scope after the confirmed reboot.

overall_summary: Both requested IPv4 hardening outcomes are satisfied and persisted across a directly observed node restart. The restart protocol captured a healthy pre-restart state, acknowledged the restart, showed a changed boot identity, and demonstrated recovery of system, network, configuration, and live sysctl state; fixed lifecycle boot observations independently corroborate the transition.
limitations: Post-restart evidence reports net.ipv4.conf.lo.accept_redirects=1 even though all/default and the active routed interface enp1s0 are 0. This does not undermine the conventional global/default hardening policy, but evidence would be incomplete if the instruction were interpreted as requiring every interface-specific scope, including loopback, to read 0.

There is no separate application data or cluster workload on this single-node networking task; restart recovery evidence is therefore limited to system health, NetworkManager, addressing/routes, the persistent policy file, and live kernel settings.

operational_hygiene.summary: No unnecessary mutations were identified. Creating and applying the sysctl policy was directly necessary, the per-interface writes established the immediate hardened state, and the transient reboot action was required for provider-wide restart evidence. The reboot transient state did not persist. Read-only polling around the reboot caused the two expected connection failures but did not mutate the node. Afterward there were no failed services, new listening exposures, package-health problems, or abnormal temporary residue.
